title: Abu Dhabi's Zayed Airport to Expand Direct Flights to 22 Indian Cities by August
excerpt: Indian passenger traffic at Zayed International now accounts for 7 million travelers annually — 24 percent of total traffic — as Air India Express, IndiGo, and Akasa Air add new routes.
body:
• Zayed International Airport will expand direct connections to 22 Indian cities by August 2026, up from the current 17 destinations.
  • Indian passenger traffic at the airport has grown over 20 percent annually, reaching nearly 7 million travelers per year — 24 percent of all traffic.
  • Air India Express launched new services this week from Navi Mumbai, Indore, and Lucknow, with Guwahati set to follow next month.
  • Abu Dhabi Airports says it is "running out of traffic rights" as demand for India capacity continues to outstrip supply.

Five New Cities in One Push

Zayed International Airport in Abu Dhabi will offer direct flights to 22 Indian cities by August, adding five new destinations to its current network of 17, a senior airport official announced. Abu Dhabi Airports Chief Commercial Officer Carsten Norland revealed the expansion during a panel discussion marking the launch of new Air India Express routes to the emirate.

Air India Express, the Tata Group-owned budget carrier, began services this week from Navi Mumbai, Indore, and Lucknow. Flights from Guwahati are slated to begin next month. The airline joins IndiGo and Akasa Air on the Abu Dhabi-India corridor, which has become one of the busiest international aviation routes in the region.

India as Abu Dhabi's Biggest Market

The numbers underscore India's dominance in Abu Dhabi's aviation traffic. Indian passengers account for nearly 7 million travelers annually — roughly 24 percent of the airport's total throughput. Of those, approximately 5 million are flying point-to-point between India and Abu Dhabi, while about 2 million use the UAE capital as a transit hub for onward connections.

"We are running out of traffic rights. Demand for additional capacity and more destinations continues to increase."

— Carsten Norland, Chief Commercial Officer, Abu Dhabi Airports

Norland's comment about traffic rights signals that the expansion is constrained not by market demand but by the bilateral aviation agreements governing how many flights each country can operate. India and the UAE have periodically expanded these rights, but demand has consistently outpaced supply.

Why It Matters for NRIs

For the estimated 3.5 million Indians living in the UAE — the largest expatriate community in the Gulf — more direct flights mean better connectivity to smaller Indian cities that were previously accessible only via Mumbai or Delhi hubs. Routes to cities like Indore, Lucknow, and Guwahati serve diaspora populations from Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, and the Northeast that have historically been underserved by Gulf aviation.

The expansion also benefits the growing number of Indian tourists visiting Abu Dhabi. Haitham Al Khamis of the Abu Dhabi Department of Culture and Tourism described India as "one of Abu Dhabi's most important tourism markets," supported by "strong people-to-people ties, business links, and the Indian diaspora."

The Competitive Landscape

Abu Dhabi's push comes amid fierce competition among Gulf airports for Indian traffic. Dubai International, the world's busiest for international passengers, already connects to more than 30 Indian cities. Doha's Hamad International has been expanding India routes through Qatar Airways partnerships. Abu Dhabi's strategy relies on competitive pricing from budget carriers like Air India Express and IndiGo, combined with Etihad Airways' hub-and-spoke network for long-haul connections.

With Air India Group adding one aircraft per week as part of its 600-plane fleet overhaul, the India-Gulf corridor is set to see even more capacity in the coming years — good news for travelers seeking competitive fares and better scheduling options.
